mainTopic: Why כל חרם is needed for one who is executed, and whether a betrothed-and-divorced נערה gets a קנס
overview: The amud opens by asking why the פסוק of כל חרם is needed to teach that someone who deserves death does not pay money for the same act. The first suggestion is a killing done with a downward motion, and רמי בר חמא suggests blinding an eye and then killing with a separate blow. רבא rejects both, because teachings of the school of חזקיה already cover them. רב אשי then says the פסוק teaches that even a קנס is not paid by someone who is executed. For רבה, who holds that a קנס is paid even then, the פסוק teaches the lesson of the תנא קמא who argues with רבי חנניא בן עקביא. A new משנה follows about a נערה who was betrothed and divorced and then violated. רבי יוסי הגלילי says she gets no קנס, and רבי עקיבא says she does and it goes to her. The גמרא shows how each reads "אשר לא אורשה", challenges רבי עקיבא, and brings a ברייתא where he uses those words for a גזירה שוה between אונס and מפתה. The amud ends by asking רבי עקיבא why he gives "אשר לא אורשה" to the גזירה שוה and "בתולה" to the exclusion, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse is needed for a killing done with a downward motion
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion continues: without כל חרם, we might think a killer who struck with a downward motion could pay money and go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that a killer cannot pay instead of dying might seem to apply only to a killing with an upward motion, because the unintentional form of that act has no atonement. But a killing with a downward motion, whose unintentional form does get atonement, might seem different. There we would say: take money from him and let him go. So the verse teaches us that this is wrong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to the question 'why do we need the פסוק of כל חרם?' It says the פסוק is needed for a killing done with a downward motion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unintentional killing done with a downward motion is punished with גלות, which works as a כפרה. Since that kind of act already has a path to atonement, we might think a deliberate killer in that case could pay money instead of dying. The פסוק כל חרם tells us he cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: An upward motion (for example, lifting the hand up)
A downward motion (for example, bringing the hand or a tool down)
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: This applies only
phrases.notes: He means the rule that someone who deserves death cannot pay money to get out of it.

phrases.english: where he killed him with an upward motion,
whose unintentional form was not given atonement.
But if he killed him with a downward motion,
whose unintentional form was given atonement,
phrases.notes: The 'atonement' here is גלות, going to an עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: say: let us take money from him and let him go,
so the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי, הֵיכָא דַּהֲרָגוֹ דֶּרֶךְ עֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began before this section, explaining why the פסוק כל חרם is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a specific case that only the פסוק could teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A killer who struck with a downward motion might be allowed to pay money and go free.
steps.terutzMaskana: כל חרם teaches that even he cannot pay instead of dying.

steps.title: רבא: this is already known from the school of חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the answer. The rule is already learned from the תנא דבי חזקיה, which compares striking a person to striking an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: This is already learned from what the school of חזקיה taught. They taught: 'one who strikes a person' and 'one who strikes an animal'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the answer in Step 1. He says there is no need for כל חרם here because another source already teaches it. He is setting up the source, which is explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a teaching already covers the downward-motion case, then the פסוק כל חרם is not needed for it. רבא names the source here: the פסוק that puts 'striking a person' next to 'striking an animal'.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school of חזקיה
It comes out of (it is learned from)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
This is learned from what the school of Chizkiya taught.
For the school of Chizkiya taught:
'One who strikes a person' and 'one who strikes an animal.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: הָא מִדְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reason given in Step 1 for needing כל חרם.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the downward-motion reason for needing כל חרם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The downward-motion case is already covered by the תנא דבי חזקיה.

steps.title: The comparison of striking an animal and striking a person
steps.stepSummary: The school of חזקיה explains the comparison. With an animal, one always pays in every kind of case. With a person, one never pays in every kind of case, including a downward motion.
steps.simpleTranslation: With one who strikes an animal, you made no difference between unintentional and deliberate, between intending and not intending, or between a downward and an upward motion. In every case he pays money and is never exempt. So too with one who strikes a person: make no difference between any of these. In every case he is exempt from paying and never has to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the content of the teaching רבא quoted. It shows that a person's killer never pays money, no matter how the killing happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק are compared. Every way of killing an animal makes you pay, so every way of killing a person makes you not pay. Since the downward-motion case is clearly listed, כל חרם is not needed to teach it.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא דבי חזקיה teaches that killing a person never leads to paying money, in any manner of killing. That is why רבא says the downward-motion case does not need כל חרם.

phrases.english: Just as one who strikes an animal:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חִלַּקְתָּ בּוֹ בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג לְמֵזִיד,
phrases.english: you made no difference in it between unintentional and deliberate,
between intending and not intending,
between a downward motion and an upward motion,
never to exempt him from paying money, but always to make him pay money.
So too one who strikes a person:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תַּחְלוֹק בּוֹ בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג לְמֵזִיד,
phrases.english: do not make a difference in it between unintentional and deliberate,
between intending and not intending,
between a downward motion and an upward motion,
never to make him pay money, but always to exempt him from paying money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מַכֵּה בְהֵמָה לֹא חִלַּקְתָּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching רבא cited in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a killer who struck with a downward motion also does not pay money
steps.raayaSupportSource: The comparison by the תנא דבי חזקיה of 'one who strikes a person' to 'one who strikes an animal'

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the verse is needed for blinding and then killing with a different blow
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא gives a new reason for כל חרם: someone who blinded an eye and then killed with a separate blow might still have to pay for the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי בר חמא said: the verse is needed. You might have thought the rule applies only when he blinded the man's eye and killed him with that same blow. But when he blinded the eye and killed him with something else, you would say: let us take money from him for the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבא rejected the first reason, רמי בר חמא offers a different case where כל חרם would be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one blow both blinds and kills, it is plainly one act, and the death penalty covers it. When the eye was damaged by a separate blow, we might think the eye is its own debt that must be paid. The פסוק would teach that even then he does not pay.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, אִיצְטְרִיךְ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rami bar Chama said: it is needed:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק of כל חרם.

phrases.english: you might have thought,
this applies only where
he blinded his eye and killed him with it.
phrases.notes: 'With it' means with that same blow.

phrases.english: But where he blinded his eye
and killed him with something else,
say: let us take money from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from Step 1 with a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new case that the פסוק is needed for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the eye was blinded by a separate blow, he might have to pay for the eye.
steps.terutzMaskana: כל חרם teaches that he pays nothing even then.

steps.title: רבא: this too is known from another teaching of the school of חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the second reason as well. 'An eye for an eye' teaches that one does not pay for an eye and also give a life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: This too is learned from another teaching of the school of חזקיה. They taught: 'An eye for an eye', but not an eye and a life for an eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רמי בר חמא's reason. He shows that another teaching already covers the blinding-then-killing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says one eye is paid for one eye. Once the killer gives his life, he does not also pay for the eye, so you never get 'an eye and a life' for an eye. That means כל חרם is again not needed for this case.
steps.whatToRemember: Both reasons given for needing כל חרם (the downward motion and the blinded eye) are pushed aside by רבא, because the תנא דבי חזקיה already teaches each of them.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָא נָמֵי מֵאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה נָפְקָא.
phrases.english: This too is learned from the other teaching of the school of Chizkiya.
For the school of Chizkiya taught:
'An eye for an eye,'
but not an eye and a life for an eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: הָא נָמֵי מֵאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's reason from Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the blinded-eye reason for needing כל חרם
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is already covered by 'an eye for an eye, not an eye and a life for an eye'.

steps.title: רב אשי: the verse is needed because a fine is a special rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that כל חרם is needed. Without it, we might think that since a קנס is a special Torah rule, one who is executed still pays it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The verse is needed. You might have thought that since a fine is something new the Torah made up, the person pays it even though he is put to death. So the verse teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא pushed away the earlier reasons, רב אשי gives a new reason why the words כל חרם are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is not payment for damage the man caused. It is a set amount the Torah decided on. Because it is so unusual, we might think the normal rule does not apply to it, the rule that a person who gets death does not also pay. כל חרם teaches that even a קנס is not paid by someone who is executed.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine: a fixed payment set by the Torah, not tied to actual damage
A novelty, a special rule that does not follow normal logic
You might have thought (introduces the mistaken idea the verse comes to reject)

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
It is necessary.
phrases.notes: He means the words כל חרם are still needed, even after the earlier reasons were rejected.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say
since it is a novelty
that the Torah introduced with a fine,
even though he is killed, he pays;
so it teaches us that he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third reason for כל חרם after רבא rejected the first two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a קנס is a special Torah rule, it would be paid even by one who is executed.
steps.terutzMaskana: כל חרם teaches that one who is executed does not pay even a קנס.

steps.title: What does רבה do with the verse?
steps.stepSummary: רבה actually holds that one who is executed does pay a קנס. So what does he learn from כל חרם?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבה, who said that since a fine is something new the Torah made up, the person pays even though he is put to death, what does he do with the words 'any חרם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבה rules the exact opposite of what רב אשי said the verse teaches. It asks what the verse means for רבה, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's reason only works if one who is executed does not pay a קנס. רבה says he does pay, so for him כל חרם cannot be teaching that. The verse must teach something else according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from this verse)
"Any devoted thing" (ויקרא 27:29), the verse being discussed

phrases.english: And according to Rabba, who said
it is a novelty that the Torah introduced with a fine,
even though he is killed, he pays,
what does he do with this phrase "any ḥerem"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב אשי's reading against רבה's opposing view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבה learns from כל חרם, since he rejects רב אשי's lesson.

steps.title: רבה follows the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: רבה uses כל חרם the way the תנא קמא does in his argument with רבי חנניא בן עקביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He agrees with the first תנא, the one who argues with רבי חנניא בן עקביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה learns a different lesson from כל חרם, the one taught by the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about this verse. The תנא קמא uses it to teach that if someone pledges the ערך of a person being taken out to be executed, the pledge does not take effect. Because רבה reads the verse that way, it is not available to teach anything about a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whatToRemember: For רב אשי, כל חרם teaches that one who is executed pays no קנס. רבה holds he does pay, so he uses the verse for the תנא קמא's lesson instead.

phrases.english: He holds like the first tanna
who disagrees with Rabbi Ḥananya ben Akavya.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא דְּרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה uses כל חרם for the תנא קמא's lesson about pledging the ערך of one being executed.

steps.title: משנה: a young woman who was betrothed and divorced
steps.stepSummary: If a נערה was betrothed, then divorced, and then violated, רבי יוסי הגלילי says she gets no קנס. רבי עקיבא says she gets a קנס and it goes to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A young woman who was betrothed and then divorced: רבי יוסי הגלילי says she has no fine. רבי עקיבא says she has a fine, and the fine belongs to her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about whether a נערה who was once betrothed still gets a קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the קנס of a נערה goes to her father. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that once she has been betrothed, the קנס does not apply at all. רבי עקיבא holds that it does apply, but because she was once betrothed, the money goes to her and not to her father.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl from age twelve for six months, who is still under her father's authority

phrases.english: MISHNAH
A young woman who was betrothed and divorced,
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
She has no fine.
Rabbi Akiva says:
She has a fine,
and her fine goes to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי: no קנס. רבי עקיבא: there is a קנס, and it goes to her.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from "אשר לא אורשה" that a girl who was betrothed has no קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי הגלילי? The verse says 'who was not betrothed.' That implies that if she was betrothed, she has no fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יוסי הגלילי's source and answers with an inference from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the קנס case as a girl "who was not betrothed." רבי יוסי הגלילי reads this as a condition: only a girl who was never betrothed gets a קנס. A girl who was betrothed, even if later divorced, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: But this implies (introduces an inference from the opposite case)

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?
The verse says: "who was not betrothed,"
which implies that if she was betrothed, she has no fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first opinion in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "אשר לא אורשה" means that a girl who was betrothed has no קנס.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reading of the same words
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads "אשר לא אורשה" as deciding who gets the money: the father if she was never betrothed, herself if she was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? 'Who was not betrothed' means the fine goes to her father. That implies that if she was betrothed, it goes to herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא handles the same פסוק and shows that he reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the words "אשר לא אורשה" teach something. For רבי יוסי הגלילי they decide whether there is a קנס at all. For רבי עקיבא they only decide who receives it, the father or the girl herself.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva? How does he read the verse?
"Who was not betrothed": the fine goes to her father,
phrases.notes: The next פסוק says the fifty silver pieces are given to the girl's father, so he connects the two.

phrases.english: which implies that if she was betrothed, it goes to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's competing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words decide who receives the קנס: the father if she was never betrothed, the girl herself if she was.

steps.title: Challenge: other exclusions in the verse mean no fine at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. The other words of the פסוק, נערה and בתולה, exclude a בוגרת and a בעולה completely, not by giving the money to them. So "לא אורשה" should also exclude completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the verse says 'a young woman' and not a grown woman. Will you also say the fine goes to the grown woman herself? It says 'a virgin' and not a non-virgin. Will you also say the fine goes to her herself? Rather, those girls are left out completely. Here too, a betrothed girl should be left out completely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא's reading by comparing it to the other limits in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק also says נערה and בתולה. Everyone agrees these mean that a בוגרת or a בעולה gets no קנס at all, not that the money goes to her. It makes sense to read "לא אורשה" the same way, as a full exclusion, which supports רבי יוסי הגלילי.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a strange result that would follow)
A woman who is no longer a virgin

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a בוגרת or a בעולה gets a קנס. Everyone agrees they do not. The גמרא uses that agreed point to challenge how רבי עקיבא reads "לא אורשה".

phrases.english: But if so,
"a young woman," and not a grown woman:
will you also say the fine goes to herself?
"a virgin," and not a non-virgin:
will you also say the fine goes to herself?
Rather, they are excluded completely;
here too, she should be excluded completely!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of "אשר לא אורשה" as deciding who receives the money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The other limits in the same פסוק (נערה, בתולה) exclude completely, so "לא אורשה" should be read the same way.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא needs the words for a different teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that "לא אורשה" is needed for a teaching in a ברייתא. There, רבי יוסי הגלילי says a girl who was betrothed and then divorced gets no קנס. רבי עקיבא says she does get a קנס, and it goes to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא can answer you: I need the words "who was not betrothed" for what a ברייתא teaches. "Who was not betrothed" leaves out a girl who was betrothed and then divorced, so she gets no fine. That is what רבי יוסי הגלילי says. רבי עקיבא says: she does get a fine, and the fine goes to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי עקיבא against the challenge from step 12. It says he uses "לא אורשה" for something else entirely, and it quotes a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed רבי עקיבא had to read "לא אורשה" as a way to exclude someone, just like נערה and בתולה do. The answer is that he does not read it as an exclusion at all. In this ברייתא, רבי עקיבא gives the girl a קנס and sends it to her father, so these words must be teaching something different.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the words are needed for a different teaching)
For what was taught in a ברייתא
A fine set by the Torah, here the fifty-shekel payment

steps.confusionAlert: In step 11, רבי עקיבא said the קנס goes to the girl herself. In this ברייתא, רבי עקיבא says it goes to her father. These are two different reports of what he holds. Do not try to make them say the same thing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva can say to you:
These words, "was not betrothed," he needs
for what was taught in a baraita:
"Who was not betrothed"
leaves out a girl who was betrothed and then divorced,
so that she gets no fine;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לָהּ קְנָס,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: she does get a fine,
and her fine goes to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 12 by giving "לא אורשה" a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words are needed for something else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא would have to read "לא אורשה" as an exclusion, just like נערה and בתולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא does not read these words as an exclusion at all. He uses them for a separate teaching found in a ברייתא.

steps.title: Logic shows the father gets the fine
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא proves with logic that the father gets the קנס even though she was once betrothed and divorced. The father gets the money from her later betrothal, and he gets her קנס money too, so the two work the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And logic shows this: Her father is entitled to her betrothal money, and her father is entitled to her fine money. Even though she was betrothed and divorced, the money from a new betrothal still goes to her father. So too, even though she was betrothed and divorced, her fine money goes to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a logical argument for רבי עקיבא's ruling that the father collects the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Betrothal money and קנס money both normally belong to the father of a נערה. The earlier betrothal and divorce do not stop the father from getting the money of a new betrothal. So they should not stop him from getting the קנס either. This sets up the next step: if logic already proves this, why does the פסוק need to say "אשר לא אורשה"?

keyTerms.meaning: And logic shows (it makes sense that)

phrases.english: And logic shows it:
since her father is entitled to her betrothal money,
and her father is entitled to her fine money.
Just as her betrothal money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה — לְאָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: even though she was betrothed and divorced, goes to her father,
phrases.notes: He means the money from a new betrothal after the divorce, while she is still a נערה.

phrases.english: so too her fine money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְאָרְסָה וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה — לְאָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: even though she was betrothed and divorced, goes to her father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical reason for רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The father gets the קנס even if she was betrothed and divorced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to betrothal money, which goes to the father even after an earlier betrothal and divorce.

steps.title: Then why does the verse need these words?
steps.stepSummary: Since logic already proves the הלכה, the ברייתא asks why the פסוק says "אשר לא אורשה" at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say "who was not betrothed"?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. Logic already teaches the הלכה, so the ברייתא asks what job the words "אשר לא אורשה" are doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, these words do not exclude the girl. Their הלכה is also already known from logic. So the words look extra, and the ברייתא asks what they come to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse say this? (What does it come to teach?)

phrases.english: If so,
why does the verse say "who was not betrothed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 14: if logic proves the halacha, the words seem extra.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the words "אשר לא אורשה" teach, if logic already gives the הלכה?

steps.title: The words are free for a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The words "אשר לא אורשה" are free, so they are used for a גזירה שוה. The same words appear by מפתה in שמות. From אונס, מפתה learns that the payment is fifty. From מפתה, אונס learns that the payment is in shekels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words are free, so we can compare and learn a גזירה שוה from them. It says here "who was not betrothed," and it says there "who was not betrothed." Just as here it is fifty, there too it is fifty. And just as there it is shekels, here too it is shekels.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra words are there to link אונס and מפתה through a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the words are not needed for anything in their own place, they are "free" to build a גזירה שוה. Each case teaches the other the detail it is missing. אונס gives מפתה the number fifty, and מפתה gives אונס the fact that the payment is in shekels.

keyTerms.meaning: Free (extra words, open to be used for a גזירה שוה)
Learning one case from another because the Torah uses the same words in both
Here / there (the two places where the same words appear)
Shekels (the type of coin used for the payment)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, "אשר לא אורשה" is a free phrase. It links אונס and מפתה so that both pay fifty shekels.

phrases.english: It is free,
phrases.notes: 'Free' means these words aren't needed for their own case, so they're open to be used for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.aramaic: לְהַקִּישׁ לוֹ וְלָדוּן הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה:
phrases.english: so we can compare to it and learn a verbal analogy from it:
it says here "who was not betrothed,"
and it says there "who was not betrothed."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:15, the case of the מפתה.

phrases.aramaic: מָה כָּאן חֲמִשִּׁים — אַף לְהַלָּן חֲמִשִּׁים,
phrases.english: Just as here it is fifty, there too it is fifty,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה לְהַלָּן שְׁקָלִים — אַף כָּאן שְׁקָלִים.
phrases.english: and just as there it is shekels, here too it is shekels.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֶה, לְהַקִּישׁ לוֹ וְלָדוּן הֵימֶנּוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words are free, and they create a גזירה שוה that links אונס and מפתה: both pay fifty, and both pay in shekels.

steps.title: Why did רבי עקיבא choose these words for the גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבי עקיבא why he uses "אשר לא אורשה" for the גזירה שוה and "בתולה" to exclude a בעולה. Why not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, what did you see that made you use "who was not betrothed" for the גזירה שוה, and "virgin" to exclude a girl who is not a virgin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבי עקיבא divides up the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both phrases could have been used either way. "בתולה" could have been the free word for the גזירה שוה, and "לא אורשה" could have excluded someone. The גמרא wants a reason for the choice רבי עקיבא made.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why choose this way over the other way?)
A girl who is not a virgin

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva,
what did you see
that "who was not betrothed" is for the verbal analogy,
and "virgin" is to exclude a girl who is not a virgin?
phrases.notes: He's really asking: why not flip it, and use "בתולה" for the גזירה שוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how step 16 assigns the words of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: How רבי עקיבא divides the words of the פסוק: which phrase builds the גזירה שוה and which phrase excludes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either phrase could do either job, so his choice needs a reason.
